market_holds: Spot $10.885 at the 2026-11-17 seal. The front-expiry straddle implies about 16.6% for the event, against a 14.4% median absolute reaction over the last 7 prints, only 1 of which was up (sealed baseline). Run-up: +7.0% over 5 days and +14.5% over 20 days. On my own arithmetic from Yahoo daily closes, the stock went from $9.16 on 11-06 to $10.90 on 11-17 (+19%), while SMPL rose 4.7%, XLP 1.9% and SPY fell 0.6%. So most of the late run-in is the stock's own and has no dated news behind it; I found only routine 13G filings and nothing since 11-10. It is still 67% below its 52-week high. Q4 consensus is EPS $0.21 on revenue of about $653M (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-10). The company guided Q4 sales flat at the midpoint (Q4 FY25 was about $648M) and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of about 10%; the FY26 guide is net sales $2.335-2.375B and Adjusted EBITDA $275-295M. FY27 consensus (S&P Global via stockanalysis, updated 2026-11-03, 15 analysts) is revenue $2.38B (+0.7%) and EPS $1.31 (+25% on $1.04), so the Street already assumes a solid margin recovery. Short interest is about 10.6% of float at 2.7 days to cover (as of 2026-10-27). The stock trades on the outlook: May 2026 fell 38.8% and Feb 2026 fell 14.4%, both on guidance. The line tomorrow is new CEO Axelrod's first FY27 guide.
view: This print turns on one number: the first FY27 guide from a CEO who started on 2026-07-29. On the Q3 call he said he was 'not satisfied with our financial performance', that he would spend months on the 'structural earning power of the business', and that he was not ready to 'put a stake in the ground' on margins. The CFO committed only to FY27 EBITDA margins that 'will improve'. The inputs to that guide lean against the +25% EPS the Street carries. The double-digit price rise on shakes comes with management's own elasticity estimate of 'slightly greater than one', so volume falls more than price rises and revenue is roughly flat to down. Whey and milk-protein inflation is 'mid-single-digit' and expected to stay elevated through next year, and freight carries into FY27. Fairlife grew double digits again in Coca-Cola's Q3 (2026-10-27), and Costco has a private-label RTD shake in Canada. The tailwinds are real but small: about 120bp of non-recurring FY26 inventory charges drop out, plus $10-12M of savings. A new CEO resetting the bar, plus a growing competitor, points to a guide at or below a $1.31 consensus rather than above it. The counterweight is real too. The stock is already 67% off its high at roughly 8-9x trough EBITDA, about 10% of the float is short, and the nearest peer, Simply Good Foods, guided FY27 sales down 13-17% on 10-27 and still rallied about 11% that day and about 27% over the week. That shows a depressed protein name can take a kitchen-sink reset as a clearing event. BRBR has already run 19% into the print with no news, so some of that relief is priced, and per P6 a run-up makes a good print move less and a bad one more. Net: a slight lean down, not enough to bet. The move will be large either way.
unpriced: Possibly the gap between a +25% FY27 EPS consensus and what the company's own disclosed inputs support (elasticity above 1, continuing protein inflation, a new CEO's incentive to reset). But a 19% run-up into a straddle of about 16.6% means the market knows the outcome is binary, and the SMPL analog shows a reset can be bought. I cannot show the gap is mispriced in one direction with enough confidence to call it unpriced.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the first FY27 guide. Its disclosed inputs (elasticity above 1, mid-single-digit protein inflation, the new CEO's 'structural earning power' review, fairlife growing double digits) lean below a +25% EPS consensus. A 19% run-up with no news adds downside asymmetry. Against that, high short interest, a trough valuation and SMPL's rally on a far worse reset show that a weak guide can still be bought. That leaves me well short of 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An FY27 Adjusted EBITDA guide whose midpoint is at or above about $320-330M (EPS of $1.30 or more), or a multi-year margin target alongside it, would likely set off a squeeze-driven rally of 15% or more.

self_critique: The strongest case against: a stock down 67% with 10% short interest, a +25% EPS consensus that may already be a stale number the buy-side ignores, and a new CEO who can blame the predecessor for FY26 is the classic setup for 'less bad, credible plan' rallies. SMPL showed exactly that three weeks ago in the same category. The 19% run-in may be buy-side positioning for that outcome, not a raised bar. Q4 may also beat on sales because retailers bought ahead of the price rise. I cannot see the guide, and my lean down rests on reading management's wording and a consensus figure of uncertain quality.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition was useful: it showed the late run-up is the stock's own, not sector beta. P7's 'estimate the line from its inputs' gave a lean but no conviction, because the deciding variable (the reaction to a reset guide at trough valuation) depends on positioning that cannot be observed. The peer analog (SMPL) pulled hard against the input arithmetic, and the playbook gives no rule for weighing the two.
